statement: You are given an undirected graph: the vertex count n (vertices 0 to n − 1) and a list of edges [u, v]. The graph may be split into several components that are not connected to each other.

The graph is bipartite when its vertices can be divided into two groups so that every edge joins a vertex in one group to a vertex in the other. Equivalently, the vertices can be given two colours with no edge joining two vertices of the same colour.
Return true if the graph is bipartite and false otherwise.

examples.explanation: Put 0 and 2 in one group and 1 and 3 in the other. Every edge of the square joins the two groups.
In a triangle, 0 and 1 must differ and 1 and 2 must differ, which forces 0 and 2 into the same group, yet they share an edge.
There are two separate components. Each is a path, and a path can always be coloured alternately.

constraints: No edge joins a vertex to itself, and no edge is listed twice
